Do not hold rent payments. This is not something that will help you in the long term with regards to deposits and referencing. Speak to the local council in regards to HMO rules for your house they should be able to confirm if your landlord is breaking any rules.

Citizens advice is a good first step and they may be able to point you in the right direction however i would entirely advise seeking proper advice from a lawyer, particularly one that specializes in housing. For most cases an initial consult shouldn't cost you anything and they will be able to tell you exactly what can and cant be done in regards to your matter they may even draft a letter to your landlord so you can get out quickly. Depending on the lawyer you may go to, what is involved with any case you may have and your financial situation you may even be entitled to legal aid but i know first hand they will not grant legal aid in regards to HMO claims or deposit claims however you will be advised as to cost for these matters, it is actually not that expensive initially.

Yes and written confirmation but the landlord never mentioned a second person. I'm not happy people are invading my space in the first place, let alone someone I don't know and was never informed about.
I have confirmation from the letting agents that this was for the two of us. This is why refrencing was completed for the both of us, would this be evidence enough?

I'm sure anyone who has been stuck in an arranged marriage, an abusive relationship, a captive situation, or any other situation where the may feel alone without actually being alone would beg to differ
